newsitem.title: USA: Knight-Ridder to buy ABC Inc newspapers.
newsitem.headline: Knight-Ridder to buy ABC Inc newspapers.

text.p: Knight-Ridder Inc said Friday it had reached an agreement with the Walt Disney Corp to buy four newspapers owned by ABC Inc for $1.65 billion.
It also said it was going to divest Knight-Ridder Information Inc, its on-line information service for business and professional users, which includes Dialog and DataStar.
"The company anticipates completing the sale during 1997," it said. "The transactions will enable Knight-Ridder to focus on its core newspaper business, which is the foundation of the company."

"The proposed transactions will result in approximately 10 percent dilution to Knight-Ridder during the first 12 months, minimal dilution during the second year and will be accretive to earnings during the third year," it said. "The entire dilution in 1997 is caused by the amortization of goodwill from the transaction."
Knight-Ridder said the $1.65 billion purchase price is less than 11 times anticipated cash flows for 1997, adding that the deal should close within 60 days.
The ABC newspapers include The Kansas City Star, the Fort Worth and Arlington Star-Telegrams, the Belleville (Illinois) News-Democrat and The Times Leader in Wilkes-Barre, Pennsylvania, it said.
Revenue for the group was $500 million in 1996, it added.
Knight-Ridder is an international communications company engaged in newspaper publishing, business news and information services, among other things.
